guide.title: System Guide
guide.subtitle: How to use the Río Texas Resolution Tracking System
guide.overviewBody: This system tracks resolutions from initial submission through committee review and Uniting Table action, to either inclusion in the pre-conference journal or not advancing with explanation.
guide.overviewPipeline: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → UNDER REVIEW → RECOMMENDED / NOT RECOMMENDED → APPROVED or NOT ADVANCED
guide.overviewFinancial: Resolutions with financial implications are automatically detected and flagged for Finance & Administration review per Standing Rule SR-14.
guide.testResolutionsDesc: Eight resolutions are loaded at various pipeline stages:
guide.petitionerStep1: Go to Resolutions → New Resolution. Fill in the title, full text, and rationale. You can write in English, Spanish, or both. Click Save as Draft.
guide.petitionerStep2: From the resolution detail page, review your text. You can click Edit to make changes while it's still a draft. When ready, click Submit Resolution. A display number (RT-2026-XXXX) is automatically assigned.
guide.petitionerFinancialWarning: If your resolution mentions dollar amounts, budgets, or financial terms, it will be automatically flagged for Finance committee review per Standing Rule SR-14.
guide.petitionerStep3: Your Dashboard shows all your resolutions with their current status. Click any resolution to see the full detail, including committee recommendations and Uniting Table decisions as they happen.
guide.petitionerTry: Roberto has a draft resolution on Disaster Preparedness that hasn't been submitted yet. Log in as delegado@riotexas.org to edit and submit it.
guide.chairLogin: Login as chair-csr@riotexas.org (Church & Society) or chair-bot@riotexas.org (Board of Trustees)
guide.chairStep1: Your Dashboard shows resolutions assigned to your committee that are in Under Review status. These are the ones waiting for your recommendation.
guide.chairStep2: Click on a resolution to read the full text, rationale, and petitioner information. Both English and Spanish versions are displayed if available.
guide.chairStep3: At the bottom of the resolution detail page, you'll see the Record Recommendation panel. Write your committee's notes, then click either Recommend or Do Not Recommend.
guide.chairStep3Follow: Your recommendation and notes are recorded with a timestamp and become part of the resolution's permanent record.
guide.chairTry1: As chair-csr: RT-2026-0002 (Climate / Creation Care) is waiting for your recommendation.
guide.chairTry2: As chair-bot: RT-2026-0003 and RT-2026-0004 have already been reviewed — see what those recommendations look like.
guide.secretaryStep1: Your Dashboard shows all resolutions across all stages. The stats cards give you a quick count of drafts, in-progress, and completed resolutions. The Resolutions page shows the full list with search.
guide.secretaryStep2: Open any Submitted resolution. You'll see the Assign to Committee panel with a dropdown of all 11 committees. Select the appropriate committee and click assign.
guide.secretaryFinancialWarning: Financial flag: If the system auto-detected financial language, you'll see an amber banner at the top citing Standing Rule SR-14 and the specific terms detected. You can Dismiss if it's a false positive, or note it when assigning to the appropriate committee. If the system missed financial language, use the Flag for Finance review link.
guide.secretaryStep3: After a committee records its recommendation, you record the Uniting Table decision. Open the resolution and you'll see buttons to either Approve for Journal (includes it in the pre-conference journal) or Do Not Advance (with an explanation that goes back to the petitioner).
guide.secretaryStep4: When a committee does not recommend a resolution, you can still record a Uniting Table decision — typically choosing not to advance, with the committee's reasoning included.
guide.secretaryTry1: RT-2026-0001 (ICE / Sanctuary) is submitted with a financial flag — assign it to Church & Society (CSR).
guide.secretaryTry2: RT-2026-0003 (Mental Health) is recommended — record a Uniting Table decision (approve or do not advance).
guide.secretaryTry3: RT-2026-0004 (Property Trust Clause) was not recommended — choose not to advance it, with explanation.
guide.adminFullAccess: The Admin role has the same capabilities as the Conference Secretary — you can assign committees, record recommendations, and make Uniting Table decisions. This provides backup coverage and oversight.
guide.adminSee2: Financial flag banners and SR-14 citations
guide.adminSee3: All committee recommendations and UT decisions

submit.title: Submit a Resolution
submit.introText: Thank you for preparing a resolution for the Río Texas Annual Conference. This guided process will walk you through submitting your proposal into the system.
submit.processStep1: Your resolution is received by the Conference Secretary.
submit.processStep2: It is assigned to the appropriate committee for review.
submit.processStep3: The committee makes a recommendation to the Uniting Table.
submit.processStep4: The Uniting Table decides whether to include it in the pre-conference journal.
submit.beforeYouStartText: You should have already discussed your resolution with the Assistant to the Bishop before submitting it here. If you haven't, please reach out to their office first.
submit.need2: The full text (WHEREAS clauses and RESOLVED clauses)
submit.need3: A brief rationale explaining why this resolution matters
submit.accountExplanation: Create an account so you can track your resolution's progress. If you already have an account, enter your email and password and click 'Existing Account'.
submit.name: Full Name
submit.writeExplanation: You may write in English, Spanish, or both. At least one language is required for the title and text.
submit.reviewExplanation: Please review your resolution carefully. Once submitted, it cannot be edited.
submit.submitted: Your resolution has been submitted! You will receive a resolution number.
submit.needTitle: Please enter a title in at least one language.
submit.needText: Please enter the resolution text in at least one language.
